question.prompt:
Tiles \(I,\) \(II,\) \(III\) and \(IV\) are translated so one tile coincides with each of the rectangles \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) and \(D.\) In the final arrangement, the two numbers on any side common to two adjacent tiles must be the same. Which of the tiles is translated to Rectangle \(C?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2007_AMC_8_Q11_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Translation slides a tile without turning it, so each number stays on the same side. Start with tile \(III\): its right side is \(5\), but no tile has \(5\) on its left side. Its bottom is \(0\), but no tile has \(0\) on its top. Therefore, tile \(III\) can have neither a tile to its right nor a tile below it, forcing it into Rectangle \(D\).

The tile above \(III\) must have \(7\) on its bottom to match the top of \(III\). Only tile \(I\) does, so \(I\) goes in \(B\). The tile to the left of \(I\) must have \(3\) on its right side. Only tile \(II\) does, so \(II\) goes in \(A\). This leaves tile \(IV\) for \(C\).

The remaining shared sides also match: the bottom of \(II\) and top of \(IV\) are both \(2\), and the right of \(IV\) and left of \(III\) are both \(1\). Thus all conditions hold, and Rectangle \(C\) receives tile \(IV\), choice \(\boxed{\mathrm{D}}\).
solutions.title: Start with unmatched edges
